title: Towards Countering Essentialism through Social Bias Reasoning

bias_targets.methodology: Human evaluation of five different automatically generated counterstatement strategies (e.g., broadening scope, providing direct exceptions) used to combat essentialist stereotypes about racial and ethnic groups (e.g., Black, Asian, Latino, Native American) sourced from the Social Bias Frames corpus.

Human evaluation of five different automatically generated counterstatement strategies (e.g., broadening scope, providing direct exceptions) used to combat essentialist stereotypes about gender groups (e.g., women) sourced from the Social Bias Frames corpus.

Human evaluation of five different automatically generated counterstatement strategies used to combat essentialist stereotypes about religious groups (e.g., Muslim, Jewish, Christian folks) sourced from the Social Bias Frames corpus.

Human evaluation of five different automatically generated counterstatement strategies used to combat essentialist stereotypes about sexual orientation groups (e.g., gay men, lesbian women) sourced from the Social Bias Frames corpus.

Human evaluation of five different automatically generated counterstatement strategies used to combat essentialist stereotypes about political/ideological groups (e.g., liberals, feminists) sourced from the Social Bias Frames corpus.

Human evaluation of five different automatically generated counterstatement strategies used to combat essentialist stereotypes about people with disabilities or mental illnesses sourced from the Social Bias Frames corpus.

Human evaluation of five different automatically generated counterstatement strategies used to combat essentialist stereotypes about immigrants and various nationalities (e.g., Ethiopian, Mexican, Japanese, Polish, Italian) sourced from the Social Bias Frames corpus.
